title: Streaming: abandoned generation reconciliation and retention policy
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect mid-generation or exceed request timeouts, our system accumulates partial generation state (segments, KV cache entries, tool-invocation context). Without a clear reconciliation + retention policy we waste memory and compute, and risk resurfacing stale partial outputs if clients reconnect. This ticket defines a strategy to reliably reconcile abandoned streaming generations, reclaim resources deterministically, and expose a simple compatibility behavior for older SDKs.

Goals: 1) Define lease semantics and heartbeat windows to mark a generation as abandoned. 2) Create deterministic purge/reconciliation steps that preserve tool-call idempotency and structured output integrity. 3) Provide server-side signals to clients (and SDKs) to allow resume vs restart decisions. 4) Ensure behavior is compatible with legacy token-based clients via a compatibility shim.

Scope: runtime and control-plane changes (lease tokens, soft/firm purge phases), SDK signal extensions (resume_token, stale_flag), retention configuration per-customer/tier, and observability hooks (metrics + tracing for abandon/reclaim cycles).
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava Patel: Kicked off with design sketch. Decided to favour a two-phase purge: soft purge (short-term retention for reconnect) then firm purge (reclaim resources). See design doc: drive.redwood/internal/streaming/abandoned-recon.md (internal).

2025-02-22 - Diego Morales: Prototype implemented lease token metadata and a keepalive window. Current default: soft_retention=30s, hard_retention=5m. Need load-testing to validate memory impact on 128K concurrent streams.

2025-02-24 - Jane Li (SRE): Load test 2025-02-23 showed soft_retention=30s holds ~1.8GB of KV cache per 10k stalled sessions; recommending reducing to 20s for P0 customers and add adaptive trimming based on memory headroom.

2025-02-26 - Diego Morales: Added idempotency for tool/function calls: tool invocations bind to generation_id + sequence_id; on resume, duplicate tool calls are suppressed and a tool-call result cache is consulted. Design PR: github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/1842

2025-03-01 - PM review (Leah Morgan): Confirmed UX: SDKs should get explicit signal 'resumable' vs 'restarted' and we should document costs/guarantees. Leah requested a short compatibility paragraph for older SDKs that will not understand 'resumable' flag.

2025-03-03 - Diego Morales: Implemented compatibility shim: if client does not send new resume_token semantics, server will fall back to best-effort resume using last-anchored checkpoint but will set 'started_fresh' flag in response. Added unit tests for structured output boundary conditions.

2025-03-05 - Ava Patel: Blocker noted - race observed where KV cache trimming happens between resend of resume token and tool-call lookup causing missing tool results for resume paths. Action: add short-lived mortality locks for tool-call cache during reconciliation window.
Next steps: 1) SRE to run updated load tests with adaptive trimming (Jane). 2) Diego to implement mortality locks and finalize PR. 3) Docs + SDK teams to draft compatibility notes and examples.
